_comment: EXT-63 SMOKE, arm 2 — identical to _ext63_gps_dual_20ep.json plus ONE key:
network.sbasis_complete.  Arm 1 produced ZERO solution epochs with a single, PERSISTENT
near-null direction:
every one of the 20 epochs: 'observed 1 (near-)zero eigenvalue below ~2.24e-04 but the
declared S-basis dimension is 0', smallest ev pinned at 1.321-1.337e-04 (lambda_max
~2.24e+05, so lambda_min/lambda_max = 5.9e-10 against the 1e-9 rank_gate_tol).
READ THE SIGNATURE.  It is NOT the intermittent per-satellite channel-family PB<->iono
trade the SBC card was built for (0-3 per epoch, 41% of epochs, GPS+Gal only).  It is ONE
direction, on EVERY epoch, at an essentially CONSTANT eigenvalue — a fixed structural
gauge that the declared dimension does not count, and its eigenvalue is only 1.7x below
the cutoff, i.e. MARGINAL rather than a machine-zero orphan (Card PA's class).  PA fired
on exactly 1 of 20 epochs (G22/L1C, span -0.000000) and recovered 0: the direction has
essentially no phase-bias span, which is why the phase-only heal cannot reach it.
WORKING HYPOTHESIS (this arm tests it by NAMING the direction, not by assuming it).
EXT-CB removes the satellite code-bias columns AND with them the per-(constellation,
signal) sum-to-zero code-bias gauge.  That gauge was the only thing anchoring the
receiver-DCB <-> global-ionosphere-level direction: with satellite DCBs supplied
externally, a common shift of every station's rx DCB trades against the SH field's mean
(a00), and the per-station rx DCB is a LOCAL state (Schur-eliminated), so in the SHARED
border the surviving half of that direction should appear as SH coefficients.  The
loader's own claim — 'Every coefficient carries a Kaula prior (a00 loose: 15+-30 TECU) so
the null-space rank gate stays at #constellations regardless of coverage' — is then
FALSIFIED for this posture: 1/30^2 leaves the direction 1.7x short.
WHAT TO READ: the sbc_engage event's per-column attribution in network_events.csv (tier
GATE).  If it is dominated by SH coefficients, the hypothesis holds and the principled
fix is a RECEIVER-DCB DATUM (the standard IGS zero-mean-over-receivers convention that
replaces the satellite-DCB zero-mean we just gave away), not a tighter iono prior and not
a looser rank tolerance.  If it is dominated by CLK or PB columns instead, the hypothesis
is wrong and the clock hold / phase-bias gauge interaction is the real story.
WHY SBC IS THE SAFE PROBE: it folds ONE minimum-constraint gauge row per extra direction
(the direction's own unit eigenvector, RHS = the carried level, 0 on cold), which is
S-transform invariant — every ESTIMABLE quantity is untouched by construction.  The
caveat is honest: at 5.9e-10 this direction is weak-but-possibly-REAL rather than an
exact gauge, so a pin there discards weak information.  That is acceptable for a
diagnostic arm and is exactly why the fix is not being promoted from this run.
PA stays armed as the backstop.  Default-OFF elsewhere, so no other arm is affected.
